newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firmer as U.S. rates woes fade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firmer as U.S. rates woes fade.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended midsession strength at the close of trade on Monday after the market discounted the potentially adverse effects of possible forthcoming hikes in U.S. interest rates, traders said.
"Many brokers do not expect U.S. rates to rise, although dealers have on the whole squared (dollar) positions to guard against surprises," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.7 and 1.85 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9090/7.9120 and 7.9040/7.9090 per dollar.
The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on May 20 to determine U.S. interest rate policy.
Dealers said they would closely watch U.S. economic data released during the remainder of the week for possible signs of inflationary pressure and subsequent tightening in U.S. monetary policy.
"Even if they (the FOMC) raise U.S. rates, the market has already discounted any increase of up to 25 basis points," another trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 2.1 centavos weaker at 7.9160/7.9180 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso would be influenced in early trade on Tuesday by the U.S. bond market's reaction to retail sales data.
